reasoning: Subject of ἐγένετο: “a thought occurred” [TREE].

Dative of the person with γίγνομαι: “a thought came to be ours”, the dative of the possessor [SMYTH:1476] [CONV:R2]. Read with the mental noun ἔννοια it could also be the person who experiences the thought (DatExpr), and Miller's “occurred to us” allows that [TR]; the possessive construction with γίγνομαι is the more regular one. Tree: the tree attaches ἡμῖν to ἔννοιά, not to ἐγένετο.

Aorist indicative stating a single past occurrence [SMYTH:1923]; γίγνομαι already means “come about”, so an ingressive reading adds little. γίγνομαι is middle-only and describes a change of state with no agent, the spontaneous-process middle [CONV:D3] [CONV:R1]. Indicative of a plain statement [MORPH].
ὅσαι agrees with δημοκρατίαι, the subject of κατελύθησαν, and takes its function [TREE].
Subject of κατελύθησαν in the indirect question “how many democracies were overthrown” [TREE].

Aorist passive indicative in an indirect question, which keeps the indicative [MORPH]. The aorist states the events as facts [SMYTH:1923]; the agent follows with ὑπό [SMYTH:1755], so the voice is passive.
τῶν makes the participle βουλομένων a noun, “those who wished” [SMYTH:1153]; it names a class only loosely, so ArtGener is a weak alternative [SMYTH:1124].

Genitive of the agent after ὑπό with the passive κατελύθησαν [SMYTH:1755]; the project tags this GenSep [CONV:D4] [PREP:ὑπό]. With τῶν it is a substantival participle, “those wishing” [SMYTH:2049]. Present participle outside indirect discourse: aspect only. βούλομαι is the card's own example of the mental-activity middle [CONV:D3].

Infinitive after the verb of will βουλομένων [SMYTH:1991], present for aspect, not in indirect discourse [SMYTH:1869]. πολιτεύεσθαι “live as a citizen, have one's form of government” is the middle of πολιτεύω [LSJ]; it can be read as acting in one's own interest (MidIndir) or as plain intransitive activity (Act). Tree: τῶν and βουλομένων hang on πολιτεύεσθαι; the phrase is τῶν … βουλομένων (object of ὑπό), and πολιτεύεσθαι is the object of βουλομένων.
ἐν δημοκρατίᾳ “under a democracy”: ἐν with the dative of the state one lives in [SMYTH:1687], tagged as place under the provisional rule for prepositions [CONV:D1] [PREP:ἐν].
Agrees with μοναρχίαι, a subject of ἀνῄρηνται [TREE].
Subject of ἀνῄρηνται, coordinated with ὀλιγαρχίαι [TREE].
Agrees with ὀλιγαρχίαι, a subject of ἀνῄρηνται [TREE].
Subject of ἀνῄρηνται, coordinated with μοναρχίαι [TREE].
Perfect indicative “have been abolished”, with ἤδη: the result still holds [MORPH]. The middle-passive form is passive here, with the agent ὑπὸ δήμων [SMYTH:1755].
Agent of the perfect passive ἀνῄρηνται, with ὑπό [SMYTH:1755]; tagged GenSep under the project rule [CONV:D4] [PREP:ὑπό].

ὅσοι … ἐπιχειρήσαντες names the whole group, which οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ then divide: Holden calls this “partitive apposition to ὅσοι τυραννεῖν ἐπιχειρήσαντες” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:13] [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:76] [SMYTH:981]. The whole stands as subject of the clause; because no verb takes it directly, a hanging nominative (NomInd) remains possible.
Infinitive completing ἐπιχειρέω “attempt to” [LSJ] [SMYTH:1991], not in indirect discourse, so aspect only. Active verb [MORPH].

Holden–Shuckburgh renders τυραννεῖν ἐπιχειρήσαντες “after setting up a despotism” [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:76]: a temporal circumstantial participle with ὅσοι [SMYTH:2054]. Without an article it is not attributive, though “those who attempted” is close. Its case follows ὅσοι (see there) [SMYTH:981].
οἱ μέν … οἱ δέ “some … others”: the article as demonstrative [SMYTH:1107], dividing ὅσοι, as Holden notes [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:13].
αὐτῶν “of them” with οἱ μέν: the genitive of the whole from which a part is taken [SMYTH:1306]. An oblique αὐτός standing alone is the personal pronoun [MORPH].

Holden: καὶ ταχὺ πάμπαν “very soon indeed: καί is intensive” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:13] [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:76]. ταχύ is a neuter accusative used as an adverb [SMYTH:1606].
Aorist passive indicative “were overthrown”, still inside the indirect question, which keeps the indicative [MORPH] [SMYTH:1923].
The second half of οἱ μέν … οἱ δέ, the article as demonstrative [SMYTH:1107].
Agrees with χρόνον and shares its function, extent of time [SMYTH:1582].
ὁποσονοῦν χρόνον “for however short a time”: accusative of extent of time [SMYTH:1582] [TR].

διαγένωνται ἄρχοντες “continue ruling”: διαγίγνομαι takes a supplementary participle [SMYTH:2097] [SMYTH:2088]. The participle agrees with the subject οἱ δέ; the tree makes it a predicate (PNOM), which is why NomPred stays as the alternative [TREE].

κἂν (καὶ ἐάν) with the subjunctive: a general condition [SMYTH:2337], so SubjSubor [CONV:D6]; the aorist gives aspect only. διαγίγνομαι is a middle-only compound of γίγνομαι, so the project classes it as a spontaneous-process middle [CONV:D3]; its sense “continue” leaves Act possible.

Present passive indicative “they are admired” [MORPH]. It states what generally happens to such rulers, so the customary present is a real alternative [SMYTH:1876]; the plain tag is kept under the project default [CONV:D2].
σοφοί agrees with ἄνδρες, the predicate of γεγενημένοι “having proved wise men”, and takes its function [SMYTH:1040].
Like σοφοί: part of the predicate of γεγενημένοι [SMYTH:1040].
Predicate noun with γεγενημένοι, a verb of becoming [SMYTH:1040] [TREE].

ὡς γεγενημένοι “as having proved”: a circumstantial participle of cause, given as others see it [SMYTH:2054]. It agrees with the subject of θαυμάζονται. Perfect participle outside indirect discourse: aspect of completed state [SMYTH:1872]. Voice as for γίγνομαι [CONV:D3] [CONV:R1].

πολλούς is what was observed: subject of the participles ἔχοντας and δυναμένους in indirect discourse after καταμεμαθηκέναι [SMYTH:2106] [TREE]. Holden–Shuckburgh notes πολλούς … τοὺς μέν … τοὺς δέ as the same whole-and-part pattern as before [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:77]. As the object of the verb of learning, AccObj is close.
Imperfect indicative “we thought”, a state continuing in the past [SMYTH:1890]. Active verb, plain statement [MORPH].
δοκέω “think” with the infinitive reports a thought: indirect discourse [SMYTH:1867]. The infinitive keeps the tense of “we have observed”, so Perf, not PerfNoni [CONV:D7].
Agrees with οἴκοις: “in private households also”, as Holden–Shuckburgh renders it [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:77] [PREP:ἐν] [CONV:D1].
ἐν with the dative of place [SMYTH:1687]; οἶκος is “household” rather than “house”, as Holden–Shuckburgh points out [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:77] [PREP:ἐν] [CONV:D1].

τοὺς μὲν ἔχοντας … τοὺς δέ: the article both makes the participle a noun, “those who have” [SMYTH:1153], and does the work of ὁ μέν … ὁ δέ [SMYTH:1107], dividing πολλούς [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:77]. The two functions coincide here, so the certainty is split.

With τούς, a substantival participle “those who have” [SMYTH:2049], in apposition to πολλούς and sharing its case function [SMYTH:981]. It describes, it does not report, so its present gives aspect only.
Agrees with οἰκέτας, the object of ἔχοντας [TREE].
Direct object of ἔχοντας “having more servants” [TREE].
τοὺς δέ (with ἔχοντας understood): the second half of the division, as with τοὺς μέν [SMYTH:1107] [SMYTH:1153].
Object of the understood ἔχοντας: “others (having) very few” [TREE].

τοῖς ὀλίγοις τούτοις “these few”: the article makes ὀλίγοις a noun [SMYTH:1153], and at the same time points back to the few just mentioned [SMYTH:1120]. Holden–Shuckburgh: “not even these few, much less a larger number” [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:77].
Agrees with τούτοις, the dative object of χρῆσθαι [SMYTH:1509].
χρῆσθαι “use, deal with” takes the dative [SMYTH:1509] [LSJ].
πάνυ τι “at all”: Holden glosses οὐδὲ … πάνυ τι as “not even these few at all” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:14]. τι is an adverbial accusative [SMYTH:1606].

After καταμεμαθηκέναι “we had observed that …” the participle reports what was learnt: indirect discourse [SMYTH:2106], so its tense keeps its time value [SMYTH:1874] [CONV:D7]. It agrees with πολλούς. δύναμαι is middle-only and fits none of the middle types well [CONV:R3].

Infinitive completing δυναμένους “able to”, not in indirect discourse, so aspect only. χράομαι is a middle-only verb of using “for oneself”, which Smyth groups with the indirect middles [SMYTH:1730] [CONV:D3].

χρῆσθαι πειθομένοις: Bigg renders it “to profit by their obedience … to maintain discipline among them” [COMM:en-bigg-1888-book1:79]. πειθομένοις agrees with the dative object τούτοις [SMYTH:1509] and says in what state they are used, between a supplementary and a circumstantial participle. πείθομαι “obey” could be read as a mental middle, as a passive “be persuaded”, or as reflexive “persuade oneself”; the evidence does not decide.
τοὺς δεσπότας “the masters”, the particular masters of these households [SMYTH:1120] [COMM:en-bigg-1888-book1:79].

Bigg: “τοὺς δεσπότας is added in apposition to τοὺς δέ for the sake of a little more distinctness, ‘I mean the masters’” [COMM:en-bigg-1888-book1:79]. So it shares the function of πολλούς and τοὺς δέ, the subject of the reported participles [SMYTH:981]. πείθομαι takes the dative, so it cannot be the object of πειθομένοις. Tree: attached as OBJ of πειθομένοις; it is in apposition to τοὺς δέ / πολλούς (Bigg).
